result.summary: Check PSBTInputSignedAndVerified for each input in FinalizePSBT before marking it complete. This ensures existing final scriptSig and scriptWitness fields are verified against standard policy flags rather than trusted unconditionally.
result.problem: When a PSBT input with a non-witness UTXO already contains final scriptSig or scriptWitness data, SignPSBTInput accepts it and ProduceSignature returns early without verifying the scripts. As a result, finalizepsbt can return complete: true and output a raw transaction hex that fails mempool verification, contradicting analyzepsbt.
evidence: PR description: 'finalizepsbt can return complete: true and a hex for a PSBT whose PSBT_IN_FINAL_SCRIPTWITNESS (or final scriptSig) is invalid.'
Author note on parity with merged fixes: '#30357 fixed the same problem in FillPSBT by checking PSBTInputSignedAndVerified, and #33014 did it for descriptorprocesspsbt.'
Included test in rpc_psbt.py reproduces the issue by flipping a bit in the witness signature of a segwit v0 PSBT, demonstrating complete: true and mempool script verify failures on master.
result.changed_since_previous: Now includes the patch: a three-line modification in src/psbt.cpp and a 28-line regression test in test/functional/rpc_psbt.py.
result.card: FinalizePSBT is updated to verify existing final scriptSig and scriptWitness data using PSBTInputSignedAndVerified before marking an input complete. Currently, finalizepsbt trusts existing final fields on inputs with a non_witness_utxo without verification, allowing it to return complete: true along with an invalid raw transaction hex that fails mempool verification. This brings FinalizePSBT in line with prior fixes to FillPSBT (#30357) and descriptorprocesspsbt (#33014). An intentional side effect is that inputs with consensus-valid but non-standard final scripts will now return complete: false.

risk.why: A flaw in script verification during PSBT finalization could falsely reject valid PSBT inputs or break workflows expecting complete: true on transactions with non-standard scripts.
